text:
Anna: quick sync — legal pushed back on the current SLA wording from the pilot contract, asking for an availability target and credits clause. can product weigh in on whether we can commit 99.9% or need to be conservative?
Mike: 99.9% seems risky for Dedicated during burst events. we can aim for 99.5% for initial GA?
Sergio: customer A will push for 99.95% in their contract, FYI. they said SLA is a gating term.
Rachel: can we do tiered SLAs by plan? hosted standard = 99.5, enterprise/dedicated = 99.9 with pricing uplift. that avoids exposing baseline to the enterprise bar.
Leah: +1 for tiering. ops/infra needs explicit latency SLOs too, not just availability. customers ask about p95/p99 latency for generation calls.
Tim: ops perspective: we can promise availability tiers, but p99 tail latency is heavily workload-dependent. better to commit to operational targets (e.g., "investigate and notify within X minutes") and publish typical latency ranges in docs.
Anna: legal wants concrete credit calculation example in the SLA doc. need to confirm the detection window and incident thresholds. Sergio, can you coordinate with contracts?
Sergio: yeah, looping in contracts. question: do we want automatic fallback clause (route to smaller model) baked into SLA for availability events? customers may accept degraded model if it's explicit.
Mike: I like the fallback idea. specify that during capacity events we may route to compatible model variant with same API surface to preserve correctness but note possible quality delta in docs.
Rachel: that means docs and SDK examples must include a migration note + sample: ```json
{"model": "compat:reda-7b-quant", "fallback_policy": "enabled"}
```
Leah: monitoring: need synthetic checks per region, per model. propose: 1 synthetic every minute for each prod model in hosted regions; alerts on >5% failure over 5m. who owns this?
Tim: eng-sre should own synthetic suite, but product must sign off on which prompts represent customer-critical paths. can product provide canonical prompt set for GA?
Anna: will compile an initial prompt set (small, cross-customer) by EOD tomorrow.
Sergio: support/readiness — we need playbooks for the top 5 incident types: capacity OOMs, KV cache corruption, model mis-serve (wrong weights), degraded perf, auth failures. Ops wants playbook owners.
Mike: I'll take "degraded perf" and "capacity OOMs". Tim takes KV cache and model issues. Leah takes auth & rollout failures. Rachel will own docs and sample code updates.
Rachel: on docs: publish two docs before GA: "SLA & Credits", "Operational Behavior & Fallbacks" plus a quickstart showing fallback flag. also an FAQ for enterprise questions (data residency, KMS).
Anna: pricing readiness — finops asked for per-token baseline and a "premium SLA" uplift. need to know expected unit cost delta for 99.9 vs 99.5. Mike can you provide cost delta estimate?
Mike: rough ballpark: to guarantee 99.9 we need extra reserved capacity and longer retention on warm pools — estimate +18-25% infra cost for Dedicated-heavy customers. Hosted mix would be lower. will send numbers.
Sergio: for contracts, recommend adding an "SLA upgrade path" clause — customer can pay uplift to move tiers mid-contract with 30d notice and capacity reservation.
Leah: support model: GA support hours are M-F 9-5 for standard; enterprise gets 24/7 with 1h P1 response. need to ensure SRE staffing or handoff to pager. oncall-bot: currently only weekday coverage exists.
oncall-bot: Reminder: current oncall rota has no weekend coverage for product-support. escalate to eng-sre if 24/7 required.
Tim: ops note — runbook readiness checklist: test runbooks in staging once, confirm playbook steps, add rollback commands, and verify logs/traces surface the right IDs.
Anna: decision points for launch: 1) SLA tiers approved + credits language 2) Docs published (SLA, fallbacks, quickstart) 3) Monitors + synthetics in place 4) Support coverage defined 5) Pricing uplift defined. we should gate GA on all five.
Rachel: timeline: docs + prompts + playbook owners by Fri. Synthetics in staging by next Wed. SLA legal signoff target next Tue. Pricing uplift numbers by Mike by Tue.
Sergio: I'll draft the addendum language for "fallbacks" and "upgrade path" and share in this thread for review.
Leah: if anyone can't meet owner commitments, call it out now. we can't ship with half-baked playbooks.
Mike: I'll send cost delta spreadsheet and a short note on capacity assumptions by EOD Mon.
Anna: thanks — I'll update the decision checklist in the shared GH issue and ping folks when draft SLA is ready. :thumbsup:
Rachel: adding a doc action: I'll add a short table comparing SLA tiers and pricing to the docs repo and share link here when ready.
Sergio: tagging contracts: @Samantha from contracts, can you review the proposed credits calc once I post?
Anna: pinging Samantha in contracts thread, thanks.
Tim: for runbook rehearsal, suggest a 1-hour tabletop next Thurs with eng-sre + product + support. we'll simulate degraded perf and fallback. anyone object?
Mike: no objections, put me down.
Leah: ok for me.
Anna: great. we'll reconvene after the rehearsal and finalize GA go/no-go checklist. thanks everyone.
